OBJECTIVE: Lexicographic laboratory ranking: feasibility, then fewer vehicles, then smaller total Euclidean distance. Unlimited fleet. Full recharge only.
INPUT_FIELDS: instance.vehicle (VehicleSpec: capacity, battery_capacity, consumption_rate, velocity, inverse_refuel_rate, start_soc)
Node: id, kind, x, y, demand, ready_time, due_time, service_time
OUTPUT_CONTRACT: solve(instance, seed, time_limit_s) returns CandidateSolution or {'routes': list[list[str]], 'metadata': dict}. Zero LLM calls in solver.py.
VISIT: Every customer_id appears exactly once across all routes (no missing, no duplicates).
DEPOT: Each route is list[str] starting and ending at instance.depot_id. Depot may appear only as first and last stop (no internal depot visits).
CAPACITY: Vehicle load never exceeds instance.vehicle.capacity along any route.
TIME_WINDOWS: Service start at each customer must respect ready_time and due_time (waiting allowed before ready_time).
SERVICE_TIMES: Service time at customers (and charging duration at stations) advances the clock.
BATTERY: Battery never goes negative. Energy from travel uses consumption_rate * distance. start_soc is already energy at the depot (do not multiply by battery_capacity).
CHARGING: Full recharge only. Station ids must appear as nodes in the returned route. propagate_route performs Schneider full recharge; full_recharge returns ChargeDecision, not float. Do not mutate StopState fields.
TERMINATION: Honor time_limit_s inside solve. Always return a routes structure even if incomplete. Loop-safe: no unbounded search without a time or iteration guard.
notes: String node ids only (never integer 0 as depot).
Do not hard-code Schneider instance ids or BKS tables.
Invent the algorithm; do not name published heuristics.
EVRPTW (Schneider 2014, 92-instance contract): visit each customer once.
